newsitem.title: JAPAN: No big reforms needed for Japan public bodies - LDP.
newsitem.headline: No big reforms needed for Japan public bodies - LDP.

text.p: Government-affiliated financial bodies such as the Japan Development Bank (JDB) still serve an important role and should be preserved in their present form, albeit with minor changes, an official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) said on Wednesday.

"All public financial bodies serve a necessary role... and they aren't going to disappear," Takamori Makino, an official for the LDP's Administrative Reform Promotion Headquarters told Reuters in an interview.
Makino said his party's Administrative Reform Promotion office would unveil a plan for reforms by the end of the current parliamentary session on June 18.

The LDP's efforts comes at a time of mounting criticism of government-affiliated financial bodies, which have been scorned for being inefficient and for straying into private-sector business areas beyond their originally stated purposes.
Makino said the specifics of the reform plan still needed to be ironed out, but he personally was opposed in principle to merging separate public financial bodies.

"The purpose of the reform is to prevent wasteful spending, and to slim down (public financial bodies) where possible... Merging or consolidating of organisations has not been the stated goal from the outset," he said.
Public financial bodies, however, should be prevented from butting into areas that private financial institutions are capable of handling, Makino said.

For example, public financial bodies should refrain from participating in syndicated loan schemes with private banks where possible, and give private financial institutions more room to operate, he said.

Regarding specific institutions, Makino said he believed institutions such as the Japan Development Bank and the Shokochukin Bank should be preserved in their present form, as they still serve important purposes.
He said that although some members of the reform panel had proposed a merger between JDB and the Export-Import Bank of Japan, such opinions did not represent the views of the reform panel as a whole.

He said the Shokochukin Bank still served an important role as a money lender to small enterprises and added that he was "one hundred percent sure" it would not be privatised, at least not in its current form.

Government-affiliated financial bodies receive loans from the Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme (FILP), which collects funds mainly through postal savings and public pension systems and then funnels them to government agencies.

According to the Bank of Japan, the total outstanding loans of government-affiliated financial institutions, including JDB, the Export-Import Bank, nine finance corporations and the Shokochukin Bank, were worth 149.39 trillion yen as of the end of December 1996.
